bugs.explanation: `list.index()` raises `ValueError` when the element is not present. Guard with `in` before calling `index`, or use a try/except block.

title: filter Returns Iterator
code:
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
odd = filter(lambda x: x % 2, nums)
print(odd[0])

bugs.explanation: `filter()` returns an iterator, not a list. You cannot index into it with `[0]`. Wrap in `list()` first, or use `next(odd)` to get the first item.

title: all() and any()
code:
nums = [2, 4, 6, 8]
print(all(n % 2 == 0 for n in nums))
print(any(n > 5 for n in nums))

bugs.explanation: `[[0] * 3] * 3` creates three references to the same inner list. Modifying `grid[0][0]` changes all rows. Use a list comprehension to create independent rows.

title: Zip Unequal Lists
code:
keys = ['a', 'b', 'c']
vals = [1, 2]
d = dict(zip(keys, vals))
print(d)

bugs.explanation: `zip` silently truncates to the shortest iterable — `'c'` has no paired value and is dropped. If mismatched lengths indicate a bug, use `strict=True` (Python 3.10+) to raise a `ValueError`.

title: reversed() Returns Iterator

bugs.explanation: Tuples are immutable — `t[0] = 99` raises `TypeError`. To change a value, create a new tuple by concatenating slices: `t = (99,) + t[1:]`.

title: Deque for Efficient Prepend
code:
from collections import deque
d = deque([1, 2, 3])
d.appendleft(0)
print(d)

title: namedtuple Fields
code:
from collections import namedtuple
Point = namedtuple('Point', ['x', 'y'])
p = Point(1, 2)
print(p.x, p.y)

title: heapq Push and Pop
code:
import heapq
heap = []
heapq.heappush(heap, 3)
heapq.heappush(heap, 1)
